persistence_invariants.brief: batch_number and serial_number are added as NULLABLE columns so a nonconforming code (AC4) can persist NULL rather than an invented value; the migration does not impose NOT NULL on them.
The (sku, location) composite uniqueness key established by F1 stays intact; the split migration writes only batch_number/serial_number and never mutates location (AC8).

The up-migration is additive-then-backfill-then-drop with no row deletes, so every pre-migration row survives (AC5, R1); the downgrade reconstructs inventory_code from location+batch+serial and restores the prior schema shape (AC7).

nfrs.brief: Existing sprint-1 stock rows survive the split migration with no loss; the additive-then-drop up path preserves every prior record and nonconforming codes are left NULL rather than dropped.
nfrs.fitness_function: Real-branch migration test (AC5, AC4): seed sprint-1 rows including nonconforming codes, upgrade, assert every row present and nonconforming rows carry NULL batch/serial.

nfrs.brief: The (sku, location) uniqueness key remains canonical; the migration never overwrites location from the code's leading segment, so no addressing collision is introduced.
nfrs.fitness_function: Real-branch test (AC8): upgrade and assert location values are unchanged and the (sku, location) constraint from F1 still holds.

nfrs.brief: Migration integration tests run against the paired Lakebase branch with Alembic applied, never a mock or in-memory substitute; CI refuses to merge a PR whose tests do not run on a real branch.
nfrs.fitness_function: pytest-bdd suite bound to DATABASE_URL of the paired branch; migration up/down exercised against real databricks_postgres; CI gate asserts no in-memory/mocked DB.

nfrs.brief: The migration is reversible: the downgrade reconstructs the combined inventory_code from canonical location plus split batch and serial and restores the pre-migration schema.
nfrs.fitness_function: Real-branch round-trip test (AC7): upgrade then downgrade, assert inventory_code reconstituted and schema shape restored.

nfrs.brief: A pre-acceptance integrity probe surfaces the count of nonconforming (unparseable) codes for operator review before the change is accepted (PO preference: no silent loss).
nfrs.fitness_function: Real-branch test (AC6): seed conforming and nonconforming codes, run the probe, assert the reported count equals the nonconforming rows.

nfrs.brief: Migration is additive where possible (PO preference): new columns added and backfilled before the old column is dropped, so ordering guarantees no in-flight data loss.
nfrs.fitness_function: Migration test asserts backfill step precedes the inventory_code drop and both new columns are populated before the drop executes.

nfrs.brief: Config in env (twelve-factor): the migration connects to databricks_postgres via the DATABASE_URL written by the post-checkout hook; the database name is not renamed or made app-specific.
nfrs.fitness_function: Config-in-env check: no hardcoded connection string; Alembic sources DATABASE_URL from env pointing at the paired branch.

nfrs.brief: N/A for this feature , R2 (no negative / no overcommit stock) is a write-time rule owned by F1's file/pick/adjust flow; this feature is a schema split that changes no quantity semantics, so the existing CHECK(quantity>=0) and no-overcommit rule are neither modified nor relaxed.
nfrs.fitness_function: N/A , inherited F1 fitness function on quantity remains in force; the migration adds no path that writes quantity.

nfrs.brief: The React SPA under client/ surfaces the split batch_number and serial_number fields; the boundary (app/routes/, renders_via react) returns JSON only. For S1 (migration) there is no UI surface; R5 is realized in the F6 story that renders the split fields.
nfrs.fitness_function: Boundary renders_via: react (JSON only); client component test asserts batch/serial render as first-class fields (verified in S3); S1 migration has no rendered surface.
